question: What is the cytoplasm and nucleus of a cell called?
solution:
The correct answer is** "Protoplasm".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cytoplasm and nucleus of a cell are called a** 'protoplasm'.**
 
• Protoplasm is the living part of the cell which consists of cellular organelles.
 
• It is a **colorless, jelly-like, viscous **substance present within the cell wall.
 
• The entire animal cell is made up of protoplasm.
 
• The word protoplasm was given by** Hugo Von Mohl.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information __**

 
• **Cytoplasm:**

 
 
• It** ​**maintains the environment which helps the different organelles to perform their functions.
 
• The nucleus contains the organism's genetic material.
 
• It also controls cell activity.
 
 
 
• ​**Protoplasm:**
 
 
• It** ​​**is made up of biomolecules like nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, etc.
 
• The protoplasm performs various functions like reproduction through mitosis and meiosis, irritability, structural support provided by** collenchyma and** **sclerenchyma cells**, transportation of nutrients, etc.
 
 
 
• **Nucleoplasm:**
 
 
• **​**It is a type of protoplasm composed of thick fluid.
 
• It contains chromatin fibers made up of DNA and found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
 
 
• **The cytosol:**
 
 
• It** ​**is the matrix of the cytoplasm and it surrounds cell organelles in eukaryotes.
